entry.title: Team ASTRO at the 2026 KIM Fall Meeting

link.title: Team ASTRO at the 2026 KIM Fall Meeting

entry.content:
Team ASTRO attended the 2026 Fall Meeting of the Korean Institute of Metals and Materials (KIM).

Prof. Kook Noh Yoon gave an invited talk in the Phase Transformation session on October 28, “Tailoring Deformation Mechanisms in Ti-Zr-Hf HCP Multicomponent Alloys via Crystallographic Control”, based on our recent Acta Materialia paper on composition–microstructure–property relationships in the HCP Ti-Zr-Hf system.

Our capstone design students also presented their first poster in the undergraduate student session (P1-18): “Microstructure and mechanical properties of Cr-Mo-W-based multicomponent alloys with Ni addition.” Over two semesters, they designed the alloys with CALPHAD, made them by arc melting, and worked on improving strength and oxidation resistance. Great work, everyone!
entry.summary: Ti-Zr-Hf HCP alloys, and capstone students present Cr-Mo-W alloys

entry.title: Team ASTRO at RQ 2026 in Busan

link.title: Team ASTRO at RQ 2026 in Busan

entry.content:
Team ASTRO joined RQ 2026, the 18th International Conference on Rapidly Quenched and Metastable Materials, held in Busan from August 23 to 28.

Prof. Kook Noh Yoon served on the Local Organizing Committee and presented “Evaluation of Self-ion Irradiation-Induced Hardening in F/M Steels and the Hardness Correction Using Pile-Up Measurements”.
entry.summary: The 18th International Conference on Rapidly Quenched and Metastable Materials

entry.title: Capstone design students visit KAERI
entry.content:
Prof. Kook Noh Yoon and the capstone design students visited the Korea Atomic Energy Research Institute (KAERI) in Daejeon. The students saw how materials for nuclear energy are developed and tested at a national research institute.

Many thanks to Dr. Hong for kindly showing us around KAERI.
entry.summary: A field trip to the Korea Atomic Energy Research Institute

entry.title: A new auto polisher arrives in the lab

link.title: A new auto polisher arrives in the lab

entry.content:
Our first major piece of equipment has arrived: a twin-wheel automatic grinder/polisher (TOPTECH), now installed in our lab (Room 415, Bldg. N8).

A good polish is where every microstructure analysis starts. With this machine we can now prepare metallographic samples in-house.
entry.summary: First major equipment for sample preparation

entry.title: Team ASTRO at the 2026 KIM Spring Meeting in Jeju

link.title: Team ASTRO at the 2026 KIM Spring Meeting in Jeju

entry.content:
Team ASTRO attended the 2026 Spring Meeting of the Korean Institute of Metals and Materials (KIM), held in Jeju from April 28 to 30.

Prof. Kook Noh Yoon gave an invited talk in the Phase Transformation session, “Self-Constructed Bi-continuous RHEA-Cu Composites via LMD process for Nuclear Reactors”, on why next-generation fusion and fission reactors need materials that withstand extreme environments, and how liquid metal dealloying can build them.
entry.summary: Invited talk on bi-continuous RHEA–Cu composites for nuclear reactors

entry.title: Prof. Kook Noh Yoon joins Hanbat National University

link.title: Prof. Kook Noh Yoon joins Hanbat National University

entry.content:
On March 1, 2026, Prof. Kook Noh Yoon joined the Department of Materials Science and Engineering at Hanbat National University as an assistant professor, and ASTRO Lab (Alloy design for STructural RObustness) opened its doors.

We design metallic alloys that stay strong and reliable in extreme environments. If you are interested in joining us, feel free to knock on the door of Room 510, Bldg. N8.
entry.summary: ASTRO Lab starts at the Department of Materials Science and Engineering
